title: Grouped FP32 formats: MXFP4, MBS-MXFP4, MXFP8 E5M2
formula: plain_mxfp4: y = E2M1(x/s)*s with s = floor_pow2(amax32/4) >= 2^-127; mbs_mxfp4: f = 1 + top8(6/amax128)/256, y = plain_mxfp4(x*f)/f; mxfp8_e5m2: p = max(2^e_group * 2^-29, 2^e_x)/4 + 5.421011e-20, y = clip(round_half_away(x/p)*p, +-1.75*2^e_group); contiguous FP32 [rows, cols] in and out
study_for: How a per-group scale becomes one vector instruction. Each group's amax lands in a scalar slot of `[1, SCALE_SLOTS]`; `brcb` fans those 64 scalars out into 8-column blocks, and the following `div`/`mul` reads the broadcast with `src2_rep_stride=1` while the data side steps by `REP_F`. That stride pair is the whole trick -- 32 groups are normalized by 32 different scales in a single call, with no per-group loop.

The E8M0 scale is exponent-field arithmetic, not a rounding mode: `build_e8m0_scale_s` masks `FP32_EXP_MASK` out of amax/4 and clamps to `E8M0_MIN_VALUE` (2^-127), which is floor-to-power-of-two in two integer ops. `build_e0m8_macro_factor` does the complementary trick for MBS, taking the top eight mantissa bits of 6/amax to build 1 + k/256.

MBS is the plain format wrapped, not a new one. `mbs_mxfp4_kernel_fp32` multiplies the macro by its factor, calls the same per-32 E8M0/E2M1 body four times, then divides the factor back out -- the nesting is visible in the source as literal reuse of `quantize_abs_to_e2m1_g32`. Read `plain_mxfp4` first and MBS is one extra level.

`_a2_mbs_div` in reference.py is a host model of the A2 divider's tie behaviour, keyed on the macro factor's code and the dividend's mantissa. It exists because the final `div` by the macro factor lands exactly on a representable midpoint for a handful of factors, and a reference that used plain FP32 division disagreed on those elements. When a reconstruction reference needs a hardware rounding model, this is what it looks like.
do_not_copy_when: You need the packed payload. Every output here is a reconstructed FP32 value; the E8M0 scale and the E2M1 code are internal numbers that are never published, so none of this is a byte-level conversion ABI.

Your columns are not a multiple of the group size -- 32 for the MX formats, 128 for MBS. Groups never cross a logical row and there is no partial-group path; the tail these kernels handle is a partial tile of whole groups, which is a different thing.

You want a per-tensor or per-row quantizer. The schedule is sized around a group that fits one vector repeat: 64 scalar slots, an 8-column `brcb` block, a 32-group tile and a [33, 64] UB tile whose guard row and padding columns are private. A different group geometry re-tiles all of it.
